exposure: Mode of instrumental vaginal delivery (vacuum vs. forceps)
cohort: 445 women who underwent instrumental vaginal delivery (227 vacuum, 218 forceps) at St. George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
finding: After application of instruments, 90% of CTG traces showed abnormal features, with tachycardia, baro- and chemoreceptor-mediated decelerations, and saltatory patterns being the most common abnormalities, but perinatal outcomes were good.
mod_finding: Increased baseline fetal heart rate was more common during vacuum compared to forceps delivery, possibly due to pain/pressure and resultant sympathetic overactivity, while the saltatory pattern was more common in forceps deliveries, possibly due to increased intracranial pressure and resultant autonomic instability.
